nodes.po_pomoc.text.t: Tomasz almost smiles. "I'm learning to sleep without waking every hour. Brygida says it'll pass. Hieronim says it's called melancholy. The cat says it's all nonsense. I believe the cat."

nodes.po_wydany.text.t: Tomasz doesn't lift his head. "They'll come. Today, or in a week. Pity it's on your account, that's all. The rest I couldn't care less about." And he goes back to staring at his hands. There's no bitterness in him, only the tiredness of a man after threshing.

nodes.po_zostan.text.t: Tomasz shrugs and goes back to staring at his hands. "I'm alive. That's all I can say. The rest depends on who comes through the gate next."

nodes.powitanie.options.[po_wydany].text.t: Will the patrol come for you?

nodes.powitanie.options.[q6_start].text.t: Why did you run from your company?

nodes.powitanie.text.t: Tomasz sits in a corner of the servants' quarters, wrapped in a horse blanket, staring at his own hands as if he didn't know whose they were. He talks quietly and hoarsely, like a man who kept silent so long he forgot how to speak.

nodes.q6_papiery.text.t: Tomasz takes the smith's papers carefully, as if they were made of thin glass. "Imperial seal. Near enough. If anyone asks, I'll say I'm serving somewhere else. Nobody'll check, because everybody's scared to." He smiles for the first time, crookedly. "I'll owe you."

nodes.q6_pomoc.text.t: Tomasz looks up and stares at you, as if he can't make out what sort of beast you are. "You'll help. Really? Then in return I'll show you how to move through the forest so the scouts don't sniff you out." He shakes your hand, clumsily, like a wooden paw.

nodes.q6_start.options.[papiery].text.t: I've got forged papers from the Głuszec smith.

nodes.q6_start.options.[wydaj].text.t: I'll hand you over to the patrol for the reward.

nodes.q6_start.options.[zostan].text.t: Stay here. You're safer here than anywhere else.

nodes.q6_start.text.t: "Because they told us to burn villages. Not the ones that rebelled. The ones that didn't pay their tax, because they had nothing to pay with. I was nineteen and I believed in the Emperor. Now I've got a pot of soup and a sack of questions. They're looking for me. If they find me, they'll shoot me. If they find you with the likes of me, they'll shoot you too. So what'll you do?"

nodes.q6_wydaj.text.t: Tomasz looks at you for a long time, and there's no surprise in him. "Right. That's how it's done. I gave up a few like me once, too. Here, it's all that's left of my pay: thirty groats. Where I'm going, they'll be no use to me." He presses the purse into your fist, then shuts his eyes and sits down in the corner, as if waiting for the patrol you'll send him.

nodes.q6_zostan.text.t: Tomasz nods and looks away. "So be it. Here at least I've got Brygida, and she doesn't make me answer for anything. But sooner or later they'll find me." And he goes back to staring at his hands.
